# Owned scoped null superclass fixture

A generic child passes a literal null to its original parent parameter with a
complete Comparator-super-T contract and stores its own Function-to-Comparable
field after parent construction. A default-false overload retains that same
function and scalar context. Source and SDK-parent profiles compile every unit
and compare original entries, fields, flags, metadata and Exceptions.
Frozen callers run 144 fresh JVM cases twice through direct, separately compiled,
reflection and MethodHandle routes. They observe null and function identities,
boolean state, parent/child initialization order, partial final fields, callback
inputs, opaque results and exact constructor and late failures. Six wrong
programs and six Code-preserving Signature controls guard scope and ABI.
Only owned fixture code executes. Use JDK 25 for the verification runner;
originals compile at release 8 and recovery uses its reported Java release.
